claims.statement: populateUI in JS.html evaluates user state in a strict non-commutative cascade: permanent lockout (Withdrawal_Count >= 3) first, then probation (today < Probation_End), then withdrawal cooldown (within 6 months of Last_Withdrawal_Date after the 1st or 2nd withdrawal), then enrolled (Current_Plan non-empty), then eligible default. The first matching state short-circuits the rest, so a permanently-locked user is never also shown as on probation or in cooldown.

The probation, cooldown, and permanent-lockout gates are enforced client-side only in populateUI; the server-side write functions processEnrollment, processWithdrawal, and processUpdateBeneficiaries do not re-validate these gates before writing. Only processChangePlan re-validates the 6-month plan-change lock server-side at write time. This is a known production-readiness gap.

The state cascade checks cooldown before enrolled status, so a user whose Last_Withdrawal_Date is recent but whose Current_Plan is non-blank would be shown as Cooldown rather than Enrolled. MIGRATION.md therefore requires that an enrolled re-enrollment row (states 5 and 10) have a Last_Withdrawal_Date more than 6 months in the past, or the cooldown check would wrongly mask the enrolled status.

The payroll cut-off rule: a submission made on or before the 15th of the month takes effect at the end of that same month; a submission on the 16th or later takes effect at the end of the following month. It applies only to the three payroll-deduction actions (enrollment, contribution % change, withdrawal) and NOT to investment-plan changes or beneficiary updates, which are effective immediately.

The cut-off is computed in Asia/Bangkok time in every server-side helper (getEffectiveDate, getEffectiveMonthLabel, getEditableUntil, isWithinEditableWindow) so the day boundary is correct regardless of the GAS project's default script timezone. getEffectiveMonthLabel frames the result as a salary month rather than a month-end date so emails don't read the day as a literal money-movement date.

The cut-off rule is mirrored client-side by getEffectiveDateInfo() in JS_Utils.html, which renders the effective-date banner in the enrollment wizard and change-plan modal; the backend formats a date and the frontend formats a month, but both apply the same day > 15 boundary and must stay in sync.

Only Enroll, Change Plan, and Withdraw are cancellable (CANCELLABLE_ACTIONS), and only while isWithinEditableWindow(submittedAt) is true (i.e., before the next 15th at 23:59:59 Bangkok time). Beneficiary and investment-plan actions log a SUBMITTED audit row but are excluded from the pending-transaction list because they are effective immediately and have no cancel state.

cancelTransaction re-checks isWithinEditableWindow before reverting, and a cancelled Withdraw restores the prior Withdrawal_Count and clears Last_Withdrawal_Date — so cancellation rolls back the withdrawal penalty (no count increment, no cooldown anchor persists). It restores the captured priorValues for the affected Enrollments fields.

calculateMatchTier(years) in Utils.gs returns employer match by tenure band: <5y -> 3%, <7y -> 5%, <10y -> 7%, >=10y -> 10%. The upper bound of each band is exclusive (the thresholds are <5, <7, <10, else).

The match tier is surfaced in the enrolled dashboard (infoMatch in populateUI), the enrollment confirmation letter (ctx.employerMatchPct in processEnrollment), and inversely as the vesting gate in the withdrawal modal.

Membership start date (the basis for tenure) is Hire_Date on first enrollment, but Current_Enrolled_Date on re-enrollment after a withdrawal (Withdrawal_Count >= 1). getUserProfile derives startDateForMath from rawHireDate and switches to enrollmentData.enrolledDate when withdrawalCount >= 1; the dashboard consumes memberSinceDate/tenureY/tenureM, never the raw enrolledDate column.

First_Enrolled_Date is set once on the first enrollment and never overwritten; its emptiness drives the wasFirstEnrollment flag in processEnrollment. processEnrollment sets memberSinceDate to Hire_Date when wasFirstEnrollment is true, else today (the re-enrollment date).

The 6-month plan-change lock is measured from max(Current_Enrolled_Date, Last_Plan_Change_Date). checkPlanChangeEligibility computes nextEligibleDate = mostRecentAction + 6 months and returns {locked: true, nextDate} if today is before it; processChangePlan re-validates the identical lock at write time and stamps Last_Plan_Change_Date = today on success, becoming the new anchor for the next window.
The 6-month plan-change lock applies only to contribution % (Current_Plan). Investment-plan changes and beneficiary updates are not throttled by it and are not payroll-cycled, per the cut-off rule.

Withdrawal_Count holds steady through each enrollment (0 through the 1st, 1 through the 2nd, 2 through the 3rd) and only ticks up when processWithdrawal runs, which also clears Current_Plan and Investment_Plan (blank Current_Plan is the not-enrolled signal) and sets Last_Withdrawal_Date = today. Members get up to 3 enrollments over their lifecycle.

The 6-month re-enrollment cooldown applies only after the 1st and 2nd withdrawals (Withdrawal_Count === 1 or === 2). getUserProfile computes unlockDate = Last_Withdrawal_Date + 6 months and sets isCoolingDown only if today < unlockDate and a real Last_Withdrawal_Date exists. Cooldown-vs-ready is decided purely by that date relative to today; there is no separate flag.

The 3rd withdrawal (Withdrawal_Count >= 3) is a permanent lockout with no cooldown path back. populateUI checks this state first in the cascade and shows Locked; processWithdrawal does not refuse the 3rd withdrawal (it increments the count), so the lockout takes effect on the next enrollment attempt.

MIGRATION.md formalizes the enrollment lifecycle as 9 states plus a probation flag. States 1 and 7 (never enrolled, fresh) have no Enrollments row; states 2-10 cycle through enrolled (Current_Plan set) to withdrawn (blank, count ticks) to cooldown (count 1 or 2, <=6 mo) to ready (>6 mo) to re-enroll, with state 6 being permanent lockout (count 3).

5-year vesting: the employer match is paid out on withdrawal only if tenureY >= 5 (whole years). The employee's own contributions and returns are always 100% vested regardless of tenure. This is a display rule surfaced in the withdrawal modal (JS_Withdraw.html openWithdraw), which renders two eligibility rows — own contributions always green, employer match green if tenureY >= 5 and red otherwise. The actual payout is calculated outside the app.

A user whose Probation_End (in the Users sheet) is a future date cannot enroll. getUserProfile sets isOnProbation when rawProbationDate instanceof Date and greater than today and surfaces probationEndDate for the dashboard's eligible-after message. Probation lives entirely in the Users sheet (a probation-blocked user has no Enrollments row) and is evaluated after lockout but before cooldown and enrolled in the state cascade.

Beneficiary validation (enforced client-side in validateStep step 3 of the wizard and validateUpdateBen of the beneficiary manager): maximum 5 entries; each pct >= 1; all pct must sum to exactly 100 (not 99, not 101); and title prefix, name, rel, and address are all non-empty for every row. The Add button hides at 5 entries, and the Next/Sign button enables only when the total is exactly 100 and allFilled is true.

Beneficiaries are stored as a JSON-stringified array in Beneficiary_Data, appended to the Beneficiaries ledger (newest matching row = active record). Each entry is {name, rel, pct, address}. The stored rel is an English key (Parent/Spouse/Child/Sibling/Relative/Friend; Other retired from the picker but retained in REL_LABELS for legacy display) displayed via relLabel() as a Thai-first label; relLabel is defined in two synced places (Config.gs and JS_Utils.html).

The title prefix (นาย/นาง/นางสาว/ด.ช./ด.ญ. or Mr./Ms./Mrs.) is a transient UI-only field merged into name at submit via mergePrefixes(), so the stored model stays {name, rel, pct, address} and nothing downstream changed. splitPrefix() is the inverse: on re-edit it scans the leading name for a known prefix from PREFIX_LIST and pulls it back into the dropdown so a re-save does not double-prefix. Both the wizard and the beneficiary manager call mergePrefixes right before JSON.stringify on submit.

processUpdateBeneficiaries is effective immediately (no payroll cut-off, no cancellable pending state) — it stamps effectiveDate: today in its letter context and the beneficiary action is excluded from CANCELLABLE_ACTIONS, so it never appears in the in-progress transaction table even though it logs a SUBMITTED audit row.

The cooldown/locked/withdrawal-in-progress message (#cooldownMessage) must live directly inside the Actions article, not inside #enrolledActionsGroup (which is display:none for non-enrolled users), or setting it visible would still be invisible under its hidden parent. showWithdrawalMessage renders the withdrawal timeline and the next-eligible re-enroll date there for cooldown and locked users.
